title: the bus TCP latency tooth measures the bus code, not the tree's growth
intention: Tooth (c)'s two trees hold the same set of paths and differ only in bytes, so its 10% bound measures the bus code and not how many files code_stamp walks. A planted slowdown in the code still reds it.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: tooth (c) red on akiendelllinux at +13% and +14%, and 1029d5146152's PROVED was refused for it. A paired bench on akienasus held the code fixed and varied only the tree: the gap follows the 128 extra .py files, not the code.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured: the ruler must measure the claim it names) and Law 8 (the planted-slowdown tooth keeps it a proof a hollow ruler could not pass).
how: _trees copies into each tree the paths only the other holds, so both walk the same files. A new tooth checks the path sets are equal; another plants a 2 ms sleep in the now tree's request path and requires the bound to red.

clauses.claim: the two trees the tooth builds hold the same set of file paths under cairn/ and bin/, and differ only in bytes at paths both commits hold
over the current tree, the Unix-socket p50 of the now tree is within 10% of the pre tree's, measured in the run
a planted 2 ms sleep at the top of _Handler.handle in the now tree's server.py reds the 10% bound

decisions.text: D1: _trees copies each path only one tree holds into the other (skipping any that would collide with a directory or a file parent), and prints the counts each way; tooth (d) checks the path sets are equal; tooth (e) benches a third tree with the planted sleep and requires p50 > pre * 1.10; PROVES gains this ticket's keys beside 5183005fa134's, unchanged.
